entries.text: This work of criticism dismantles a single Balzac novella line by line into five codes, enacting rather than describing the "writerly" text. Barthes's method — the granular, sequential reading that treats the story as a tissue of citations — is the argument; the book's form performs its claim that meaning is plural and produced by the reader.

entries.name: Aspects of the Novel
entries.author: E.M. Forster
entries.awards: None (predates the relevant prizes; verified negative).
entries.description: Delivered as lectures, this criticism proposes the durable distinctions — story versus plot, flat versus round characters — in a deceptively casual,…
entries.text: Delivered as lectures, this criticism proposes the durable distinctions — story versus plot, flat versus round characters — in a deceptively casual, conversational prose. Forster's accomplishment is to make craft vocabulary usable by novelists themselves; the informality is strategic, disarming theory into practical wisdom about how fiction actually works.

entries.name: The Rhetoric of Fiction
entries.author: Wayne C. Booth
entries.awards: None (no relevant prize; verified negative).
entries.description: This criticism reintroduced the "implied author" and the "unreliable narrator," insisting that even the most impersonal fiction is a rhetorical act…
entries.text: This criticism reintroduced the "implied author" and the "unreliable narrator," insisting that even the most impersonal fiction is a rhetorical act on a reader. Booth's achievement is to reopen the ethics of narration against the dogma of pure showing; the book argues that authorial choice is inescapable and that technique always carries a claim on belief.

entries.name: Narrative Discourse
entries.author: Gérard Genette
entries.awards: None (no relevant prize; verified negative).
entries.description: This structuralist criticism, built from a reading of Proust, supplies the still-standard grammar of narrative — order, duration, frequency,…
entries.text: This structuralist criticism, built from a reading of Proust, supplies the still-standard grammar of narrative — order, duration, frequency, focalisation, voice. Genette's accomplishment is a precise, transferable vocabulary for how time and perspective are managed in prose; the systematic rigour is what made narratology a usable discipline.

entries.name: How Fiction Works
entries.author: James Wood
entries.awards: None (no relevant prize; verified negative).
entries.description: This criticism argues the case for close reading in a lucid, essayistic voice, taking free indirect style and the telling detail as the engine of…
entries.text: This criticism argues the case for close reading in a lucid, essayistic voice, taking free indirect style and the telling detail as the engine of realist fiction. Wood's accomplishment is to restore the sentence and the noticed particular to the centre of critical attention; the book's persuasive intimacy is itself a defence of how literary fiction means.

entries.name: Theory of Prose
entries.author: Viktor Shklovsky
entries.awards: None (predates the relevant prizes; verified negative).
entries.description: This foundational Formalist criticism advances "defamiliarisation" (ostranenie) — art's power to make the stone stony by slowing perception — and…
entries.text: This foundational Formalist criticism advances "defamiliarisation" (ostranenie) — art's power to make the stone stony by slowing perception — and separates plot (syuzhet) from story (fabula). Shklovsky's accomplishment is to relocate the literary from content to device; the argument that form itself estranges the habitual underwrites the whole pack's "how it means" thesis.

entries.name: The Program Era
entries.author: Mark McGurl
entries.awards: Truman Capote Award for Literary Criticism, 2011.

entries.text: This literary history argues that the postwar rise of the creative-writing program is the decisive institutional fact of modern American fiction, shaping its house styles from "show don't tell" to reflexive craft. McGurl's accomplishment is to read the MFA not as decline or salvation but as a system whose pressures are legible in the work itself.

entries.name: The Art of the Novel
entries.author: Milan Kundera
entries.awards: None (no relevant prize; verified negative).
entries.description: This essay collection defends the novel as an autonomous mode of knowledge — the exploration of existence — descending from Cervantes through the…
entries.text: This essay collection defends the novel as an autonomous mode of knowledge — the exploration of existence — descending from Cervantes through the Central European moderns. Kundera's accomplishment is a novelist's poetics rather than a scholar's; the book argues that the form's wisdom is inseparable from its irony, structure and refusal of the sentimental.

entries.name: The English Patient (1996 film)
entries.author: Anthony Minghella (dir.)
entries.awards: Academy Award for Best Picture, 1997 (nine Academy Awards total, including Best Director).
entries.description: Minghella's adaptation externalises Ondaatje's fragmentary interiority into a lush cross-cut structure, using desert light, memory and montage to…
entries.text: Minghella's adaptation externalises Ondaatje's fragmentary interiority into a lush cross-cut structure, using desert light, memory and montage to approximate on screen the novel's poetic dislocation of time. The accomplishment is a rare instance of a lyric, non-linear literary novel translated into cinema without collapsing into conventional romance.

entries.name: The Remains of the Day (1993 film)
entries.author: James Ivory (dir.)
entries.awards: None won (nominated for eight Academy Awards, no wins; verified negative).
entries.description: The Merchant-Ivory adaptation renders Ishiguro's unreliable retrospection through performance and restraint, letting the camera hold on the butler's…
entries.text: The Merchant-Ivory adaptation renders Ishiguro's unreliable retrospection through performance and restraint, letting the camera hold on the butler's composed face while the audience reads the wasted feeling beneath. The achievement is a screen equivalent for interior repression, the drama carried by what is withheld rather than shown, faithful to the novel's central irony.

entries.name: Atonement (2007 film)
entries.author: Joe Wright (dir.)
entries.awards: Academy Award for Best Original Score, 2008 (Dario Marianelli) — its sole Oscar win among seven nominations; Golden Globe for Best Motion Picture – Drama, 2008.
entries.description: Wright finds cinematic devices — a typewriter woven into the score, a long unbroken tracking shot at Dunkirk — to carry McEwan's concern with…
entries.text: Wright finds cinematic devices — a typewriter woven into the score, a long unbroken tracking shot at Dunkirk — to carry McEwan's concern with narration and guilt. The film reproduces the novel's metafictional turn in its final confession, so the adaptation preserves the book's argument that the storyteller both wounds and atones.

entries.name: Brooklyn (2015 film)
entries.author: John Crowley (dir.)
entries.awards: BAFTA Award for Outstanding British Film, 2016; three Academy Award nominations, no wins.
entries.description: Adapted by Nick Hornby, the film honours Tóibín's restraint, staging an emigrant's divided heart through composition, colour and silence rather than…
entries.text: Adapted by Nick Hornby, the film honours Tóibín's restraint, staging an emigrant's divided heart through composition, colour and silence rather than exposition. The accomplishment is a screen intimacy that trusts the withheld the way the novel does, so a quiet interior story keeps its emotional weight without inflation.

entries.name: The Handmaid's Tale (2017 tv)
entries.author: Bruce Miller (creator)
entries.awards: Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Drama Series, 2017 (the first streaming series to win the category).
entries.description: The series extends Atwood's first-person testimony into a visual grammar of close-up, voiceover and saturated colour that keeps Offred's constrained…
entries.text: The series extends Atwood's first-person testimony into a visual grammar of close-up, voiceover and saturated colour that keeps Offred's constrained consciousness central. The accomplishment is sustaining, across serial length, the novel's claustrophobic interiority; the show's expansions beyond the book raise the very questions of narration and authority the novel framed.

entries.name: Wolf Hall (2015 tv)
entries.author: Peter Kosminsky (dir.)
entries.awards: Golden Globe for Best Miniseries or Television Film, 2016; BAFTA TV Awards for Best Drama Series and for Best Leading Actor (Mark Rylance), 2016.
entries.description: The adaptation seeks a visual equivalent for Mantel's present-tense intimacy, using natural candlelight and a watchful camera locked to Cromwell's…
entries.text: The adaptation seeks a visual equivalent for Mantel's present-tense intimacy, using natural candlelight and a watchful camera locked to Cromwell's point of view. The accomplishment is restraint: it resists costume-drama spectacle to preserve the novel's sense of history observed from inside one calculating mind, so perspective, not pageantry, drives the drama.
